transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately that brought you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling really down lately. It’s been a few weeks now, and there’s this kind of heavy, sad pressure that’s with me most of the day. I’m still going to work and trying to smile with my patients, so I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but inside I feel like I’m barely holding myself together.
Has this feeling of sadness or low mood been present most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific stressors?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been there most of the day for the past few weeks — like this heavy, sad feeling sitting on me. Even at work, when I’m smiling and trying to be normal with patients, inside I feel like I’m barely holding it together.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest or enjoyment in activities you used to find pleasurable, like hobbies, work, or time with family and friends?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I still get through work and everything, but after my shifts I used to paint sometimes, or go to yoga or salsa just to decompress. Lately I mostly just go home and sit on the couch. I’ll see texts from friends and think I should answer, but I just… don’t. It all feels like too much effort, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling more fatigued or lacking in energy lately, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally demanding?

I’m not totally sure… I mean, I do feel tired sometimes, but I also work long shifts, so I don’t know if that “counts.” It’s not like I’m unable to do things, exactly. I guess I’ve noticed I’m more drained than usual, but I might just be worn out? Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

A bit, yeah… I mean, I’m still doing my job, but I’ve noticed I have to reread medication orders or wound-care notes more than I usually would, just to be sure I’m not missing something. My brain feels kind of foggy.

And even little decisions that I’d normally make automatically, I’ll just freeze for a second and second-guess myself. I don’t know if that sounds dramatic, but it’s been happening enough that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating more or less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Um… maybe a little less, yeah. I don’t think it’s anything extreme, but food just hasn’t sounded that appealing lately.

I know I should be eating regularly, especially with my shifts, but some days I’ll get halfway through clinic and realize I’ve only had coffee or some crackers. I’m not trying to skip meals or anything, it just kind of happens. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping more than usual even though you’re not particularly tired?

I don’t think so… not in a way that really stands out. My sleep’s never been perfect with work schedules, so it’s a little hard to tell what’s “new,” you know?

I wouldn’t say I’m sleeping all day or anything like that, and I’m not sure I’d call it insomnia. Maybe it’s been a bit off here and there, but nothing I’ve really been tracking. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Um… I’m kind of embarrassed to say it, but… yes, sort of.

I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, and I don’t think I would do anything like that. But I’ve had thoughts like… I wish I just wouldn’t wake up. That’s actually what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment.

I hope that makes sense… I’m not trying to be dramatic, I just didn’t want to keep pretending it wasn’t happening.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or speaking more slowly, to the point that others might notice it?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t really want to call attention to it, but things just feel slower than they should.

It’s like I’m moving through syrup sometimes. Even basic stuff at the clinic—getting wound care supplies together, finishing charting—takes me longer than it normally would. I don’t know if other people have noticed, or maybe they’re just being polite, but I’ve definitely noticed it.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Would you say you’ve completely lost interest in all activities, including things you used to enjoy or even things that used to make you happy?

I don’t know if I’d say “completely,” exactly… like, I don’t want to overstate it. But yeah, it’s pretty close.

After my shifts, I used to do things to unwind—paint, or go to yoga, sometimes salsa—and those things used to actually make me feel better. Lately I just go home and sit on the couch. I’ll see texts come in and just… not answer them, because even that feels like too much effort.

It’s not that I hate those things now, I guess. They just don’t feel worth it. Does that count?
Have you had any days recently where your mood was unusually high or irritable, or where you felt more energetic or active than usual, to the point that it was noticeable to others?

No… I don’t think so. Not in that way.

I mean, I get irritable sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had days where I felt unusually up or full of energy, or like other people would notice me being more active than normal. If anything… no, I don’t think that’s been happening. Is that what you mean?
Would you say there have been days where you’ve experienced a complete loss of interest or pleasure in all activities, even ones you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I’m not sure if I’d say every single activity, completely, but it’s been pretty close.

After my shifts, I used to paint or go to yoga, or sometimes salsa, just to decompress. Lately I just go home and sit on the couch. I’ll see texts and I don’t answer them, not because I’m trying to be rude… it just feels like none of it is worth the effort.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of “loss of interest” you mean.

inference_history.note: The patient endorsed several core symptoms of depression, including depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, impaired concentration, and passive suicidal ideation. These symptoms have been present for several weeks and appear to meet criteria for moderate to severe depressive episode. The absence of a significant change in sleep patterns makes F32.0 and F32.1 less likely. F32.8 and F32.9 were ruled out due to the clear presentation aligning more with F32.2 or F32.3. Further clarification is needed to determine if psychotic features are present (F32.3) or if it remains a moderate episode (F32.2).

The patient endorsed psychomotor retardation in addition to the previously reported symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, concentration difficulties, appetite disturbance, and passive suicidal ideation. These are consistent with major depressive disorder, moderate (F32.2) or severe without psychotic features (F32.3). No features of psychosis or increased severity beyond what is captured in F32.3 have been identified to warrant a higher severity code.
